item.description:
**A host key you were being asked to approve could go unseen.** When the question did not fit the window — large text, or a narrow one — the terminal wrapped it, and the app looked for it a line at a time and found it in neither half. So nothing was asked: ssh sat on the other end waiting for an answer that was never coming, and the session showed as connected throughout. A wrapped question is read now, and what comes up is the fingerprint and the warning above it rather than the whole screen around them.
**A session said it was connected before anything had answered.** The test for "has the far side said anything" counted a terminal that had heard nothing as output, because an untouched buffer is its own blank rows rather than nothing at all. Every session therefore reported connected about a fifth of a second after it opened, whether or not the host was there or willing. It says connecting until something actually arrives.
**A download that cannot be written no longer takes the app with it.** A full disk, a volume pulled out mid-transfer, permissions changed underneath — the write that noticed raised something no Swift `catch` can see, so the app vanished where it meant to say the file could not be written.
Nothing else is visible from the outside. The suite went from 383 checks to 403, and the terminal is in it for the first time: the watchdog, what it makes of what is on screen, and the reading of the screen itself, all without a pty — the terminal is handed its output directly instead. Two of the three fixes above were found that way, by tests written for coverage rather than after a bug report.

**An empty file can be carried.** A zero-byte file — a lock file, a `.keep`, a log that had just been rotated — came back as "0 of 0 bytes arrived" and was simply uncarryable, in every release up to 0.0.3. The download side could not tell "the server said zero" from "the server would not say" and had to treat both as a failure. It can tell now, and a size the server does give has to match exactly, zero included.
**A file session that dies no longer takes the app with it.** When the `ssh` process behind a transfer went away, the write that noticed it raised an error from underneath Foundation of a kind nothing in Swift can catch — so the app vanished instead of saying the session had ended. The message it was always meant to show now actually arrives, whether the far end closed or simply stopped listening.
Nothing else is visible from the outside. The suite went from 315 checks to 383, and the SFTP conversation is now held against a server written in Swift inside the test process — one that can misbehave on purpose, answering a read with fewer bytes than its own listing promised, or replying to a request nobody made. A real server will not do either on request, and that is what turned up the empty-file bug on its first run. The host-key question and a terminal session's own bookkeeping are checked without a pty now, and a file pane's derived values without connecting to anything.

**⌘B brings the SFTP window back.** It used to do nothing whenever the host list was not the front window — including from the SFTP window itself and from Settings, which is exactly when you would reach for it. Bringing a browser you already have forward no longer needs the host list in front. Opening a *new* one still does, because that needs the host list the window holds.
Nothing else is visible from the outside. The rest of this release is groundwork: the rules behind the tab strip, Quick Connect's ranking, the group tree and the host store have been lifted into places that can be checked without driving the window, and the suite went from 254 checks to 315 — the first of them to reach above the engine. Three cycle guards, against a group becoming its own ancestor, had never been exercised until now.
The Release build compiles without a warning again, which is mostly worth saying because that is where a real one would otherwise hide.
